title: Can a code change a fit?
hook: The category stays the same when its number changes.

knows: Small arithmetic and the prerequisites listed below.
doesNotKnow: arbitrary numeric category codes inject an order and spacing into a linear fit; renaming a code can change predictions even when category identities and targets stay fixed.

misconception: arbitrary numeric category codes inject an order and spacing into a linear fit; renaming a code can change predictions even when category identities and targets stay fixed.
objective: arbitrary numeric category codes inject an order and spacing into a linear fit; renaming a code can change predictions even when category identities and targets stay fixed.

claims.text: Ordinary least squares computes slope/intercept from category-code rows. Codes[0,1,2] with targets[0,1,0] predict one-third each,SSE2/3; codes[0,2,1] predict[-1/6,5/6,1/3],SSE1/6. Independent one-hot category means predict[0,1,0],SSE0. Circle targets, square predictions and residual segments are generated from the fitted arrays.
claims.source: Local model.ts and model.repro.mjs; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.preprocessing.OneHotEncoder.html (author documentation categorical-feature encoding definition and linear-model use; local line fitting computed from rows), opened2026-10-19 for method context, not verification of toy outputs.

claims.text: Title: Can a code change a fit? Hook: The category stays the same when its number changes. Categories A, B, C have targets 0, 1, 0. Could swapping arbitrary B/C numeric codes change a fitted line? Options: Yes / No; answer 0.
claims.source: Local model.ts and model.repro.mjs; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.preprocessing.OneHotEncoder.html (author documentation categorical-feature encoding definition and linear-model use; local line fitting computed from rows), opened2026-10-19 for method context, not verification of toy outputs.
claims.address: meta.json title/hook; Demo.tsx predict question/options and locked fixture

claims.text: The retained numeric coding fits a flat prediction of one third. Swapping two arbitrary codes changes the fitted line and its errors, although the category targets did not change. One-hot coefficients fit the three category targets here. This does not prove one-hot is best for every model or unseen category.
claims.source: Local model.ts and model.repro.mjs; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.preprocessing.OneHotEncoder.html (author documentation categorical-feature encoding definition and linear-model use; local line fitting computed from rows), opened2026-10-19 for method context, not verification of toy outputs.
claims.address: Demo.tsx reveal and retained original-case witness

claims.text: A, B, C have targets 2, 0, 2. With separate one-hot coefficients and no intercept, what coefficients fit exactly? Each independent category coefficient takes its own target, regardless of arbitrary numeric codes.

claims.text: Numeric codes are arbitrary labels here, not genuinely ordered measurements. No claim of universal generalisation or automatic handling of unseen categories.
